response.sql: WITH gc AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) >= '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) <= '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender) SELECT gender, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM gc) AS above_average FROM gc WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM gc)

assumptions.assumption: Customers with a NULL gender form their own group and count as a gender group in the average (NULL-gender group is shown if it exceeds the average). Orders are joined to Customers via inner join, so orders without an existing customer are excluded.
The average is the unweighted mean of per-gender order counts, only over genders that have at least one order in the date range.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude customers whose gender is NULL from the per-gender groups and from the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH gc AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) >= '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) <= '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender) SELECT gender, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM gc) AS above_average FROM gc WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM gc)
